name: Khajuraho
description: Khajuraho is a small town in Madhya Pradesh famous for its UNESCO-listed medieval Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandela dynasty between 950 and 1050 CE. The temples are celebrated for their intricate erotic sculptures and exceptional Nagara-style architecture, though only about 20 of the original 85 temples survive. It suits history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, and photographers far more than adventure seekers or beach-goers.
nearest_railhead: Khajuraho Railway Station (KZJ) — on the Mahoba–Khajuraho branch line; most visitors change at Jhansi or Mahoba for mainline connections
nearest_airport: Khajuraho Airport (HJR) — domestic flights to Delhi, Varanasi, and Agra; roughly 5 km from the temple complex

attractions.name: Western Group of Temples
attractions.description: The main UNESCO-protected cluster containing the grandest temples including Kandariya Mahadeva, Lakshmana, and Chhaturbhuja. These represent the pinnacle of Chandela craftsmanship and are the primary reason most visitors come to Khajuraho.

attractions.name: Eastern Group of Temples (Jain and Hindu)
attractions.description: A quieter cluster comprising both Jain temples (Parsvanatha, Adinatha, Shantinatha) and Hindu shrines scattered around the old village area. Parsvanatha temple has some of the finest secular sculpture friezes in Khajuraho.

attractions.name: Southern Group of Temples (Duladeo & Chaturbhuja)
attractions.description: The smallest and most overlooked cluster, featuring the graceful Duladeo temple on the Khodar river bank and the Chaturbhuja temple with its impressive four-armed Vishnu image. Few tourists make it here, so visits are peaceful.

attractions.name: Sound and Light Show, Western Group
attractions.description: A nightly open-air show projected onto the Western Group temples that narrates Chandela history with dramatic lighting. The show runs in Hindi and English on alternate evenings; the illuminated temples make for striking long-exposure photography.

attractions.name: Archaeological Museum Khajuraho
attractions.description: A small ASI museum adjacent to the Western Group containing rescued sculptures, damaged temple fragments, and context panels on Chandela history. Useful for understanding iconography before or after visiting the temples, though the collection is modest.

attractions.name: Raneh Falls
attractions.description: A natural canyon on the Ken River about 20 km from Khajuraho where the river drops through a dramatic gorge of pink and grey granite. Seasonal — most impressive from July to October after monsoon rains; a dry-season visit can disappoint.

attractions.name: Panna National Park
attractions.description: A tiger reserve on the Ken River about 45 km from Khajuraho, known for successful tiger reintroduction after local extinction in 2009. Safaris offer genuine wildlife sightings including tigers, leopards, vultures, and crocodiles, though tiger sightings are not guaranteed.

attractions.name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
attractions.description: The tallest and most elaborately carved of all Khajuraho temples, rising 30 metres with over 800 sculptures on its exterior. Although technically within the Western Group complex, dedicating separate time to study this single temple closely rewards architecture enthusiasts.

attractions.name: Adivart Tribal and Folk Art Museum
attractions.description: A small but genuinely interesting state-run museum displaying the folk and tribal art traditions of Madhya Pradesh — Gond paintings, Baiga textiles, and ritual objects that provide cultural context far beyond the temples. Often overlooked by package tourists and rarely crowded.

attractions.name: Matangeshwar Temple
attractions.description: The only temple in the Khajuraho complex still in active daily worship, housing a 2.5-metre Shivalinga. It stands just outside the ticketed ASI enclosure and is free to enter; visitors can observe genuine religious practice rather than just archaeology.
